claim: Commonly used measures of AI metacognitive sensitivity are not independent of type 1 task performance; meta-d' from signal detection theory is proposed to address this.
stance_target: F: calibration/discrimination metrics need instrument-style validity analysis
quoted_support: This paper is primarily a methodological contribution that highlights a key limitation of commonly used measures of AI metacognitive sensitivity -- the ability to generate confidence ratings that distinguish correct from incorrect responses.

breadth.confidence_families: verbal five-point confidence ratings only (Methods); type 2 AUROC (AUC2), meta-d', M-ratio
breadth.reasoning_models: reasoning budget mentioned only as a tunable not tested (Discussion)
breadth.elicitation_formats: single prompt per item; batching and one-by-one mentioned as untested variations (Discussion)
breadth.benchmarks: SST-2 valence, oral vs written sentence dataset, deleted-'the' task; no code
breadth.label_source: human labels and constructed ground truth for the 3 tasks
breadth.calibration_metrics: AUC2, meta-d', M-ratio, SDT criterion; also states metacognitive calibration concept

claim: Experiments use three LLMs (GPT-5, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, Mistral-Medium-2508) on three non-code binary tasks with five-point confidence scales; the authors state their approach is instrumental and the article is not a benchmark paper.
quoted_support: We emphasize that our approach is strictly instrumental and outcome-oriented, making no claims about whether these systems possess genuine self-monitoring

claim: Risk-configuration prompts shift the type 1 decision criterion of LLMs toward conservative behavior in most task-model combinations.
quoted_support: These results show that, in most cases across tasks and models, we were able to induce a conservative behavior toward either S1 or S2 by specifying a risk configuration in natural language through prompt design.
